items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Short and clearly formatted, but the inline `try: domain = DNS_NAME.encode('idna')... except (AttributeError, UnicodeError): domain = DNS_NAME` has no comment. It isn't obvious that AttributeError is expected because DNS_NAME is normally a CachedDnsName object.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')` is copied into both utils.py and message.py instead of a shared helper. The message.py branch only exists to cope with tests patching DNS_NAME as a str, which duplicates the source-level conversion.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: `except (AttributeError, UnicodeError): domain = DNS_NAME` hides IDNA failures and falls back to the raw, possibly non-ASCII value, so header encoding crashes later. Using AttributeError as type dispatch is fragile.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: Converts at the source in get_fqdn (`socket.getfqdn().encode('idna').decode('ascii')`), which works for all encodings and leaves ASCII names unchanged. But it repeats the conversion inline in message() with a try/except that falls back silently.
